item.title: GloSVeT: a global 0.05° monthly mean surface soil and vegetation component temperature dataset (2003–2023)
item.description:
GloSVeT: a global 0.05° monthly mean surface soil and vegetation component temperature dataset (2003–2023)
Xiangyang Liu, Zhao-Liang Li, Chen Ru, Si-Bo Duan, and Pei Leng
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6885–6911, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6885-2026, 2026
Quantifying soil and vegetation temperatures separately is essential for understanding land–atmosphere energy exchange, drought dynamics, and agricultural responses to climate change. This study presents a global dataset providing monthly surface soil and vegetation temperatures from 2003 to 2023 at 0.05° resolution. The dataset enables detailed analyses of surface warming patterns and supports improved monitoring of hydrothermal conditions and ecosystem functioning.

item.title: A global gridded dataset of significant wave height via fusion of multi-mission altimetry and numerical hindcast
item.description:
A global gridded dataset of significant wave height via fusion of multi-mission altimetry and numerical hindcast
Haoyu Jiang and Hao Su
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6841–6858, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6841-2026, 2026
We created a global, high-accuracy wave height dataset by combining sparse but precise satellite data with computer simulations to fill gaps and reduce errors, especially for extreme waves. It's freely available in two versions: one for climate trend analysis and another for training AI wave models, providing a valuable tool for ocean research and forecasting.

item.title: Signal-domain guided deep learning for gap-filling of XCO and XCH4: a masked spatio-temporal fusion of TROPOMI and GEOS-Chem (2019–2023)
item.description:
Signal-domain guided deep learning for gap-filling of XCO and XCH4: a masked spatio-temporal fusion of TROPOMI and GEOS-Chem (2019–2023)
Chengkun An, Yuan Tian, Zhiwei Li, Qiaoyu Jiang, Peize Lin, Bowen Chang, Jingkai Xue, and Youwen Sun
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6859–6884, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6859-2026, 2026
This study addresses the problem of missing carbon monoxide and methane data in satellite observations by integrating satellite observations, atmospheric chemistry simulations, and artificial intelligence techniques to generate complete daily datasets from 2019 to 2023 with a global resolution of 0.25° and a China-specific resolution of 0.05°. The dataset can support research on atmospheric changes, wildfire signals, agricultural regions, and related environmental impacts.

item.title: A global urban built-up area dataset for cities with populations exceeding 300,000 (2000–2025)
item.description:
A global urban built-up area dataset for cities with populations exceeding 300,000 (2000–2025)
Dinoo Gunasekera, Zhongchang Sun, Wenjie Du, Jian Gao, Yunpeng Zhang, Yuyu Zhou, Robert Ndugwa, and Huadong Guo
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-381,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 1 comment)
Urban areas are expanding rapidly worldwide, but inconsistent definitions make cities hard to compare. This study created a new dataset mapping urban built-up areas for 1,611 cities from 2000 to 2025 using satellite imagery and population data. A unified definition of urban settlements allows fair comparisons across countries and time. The results show how land consumption and population growth are linked across regions, supporting global monitoring of sustainable development.

item.title: FAO estimates of net forest emissions and removals, 1990–2025
item.description:
FAO estimates of net forest emissions and removals, 1990–2025
Francesco N. Tubiello, Anne Branthomme, Griffiths Obli-Laryea, Michelle Piccoli, Nidal Ramadan, Rocio Danica Condor, Nathan Wanner, Rachele Brivio, Örjan Jonsson, Giulia Conchedda, and Anssi Pekkarinen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6799–6813, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6799-2026, 2026
Estimates of net forest emissions/removals were updated using the 2025 Forest Resources Assessment data, submitted by countries to the Food and Agriculture Organization. Results show that forests acted globally as sinks of atmospheric carbon, despite ongoing losses due to deforestation.  Results were consistent with country data independently submitted under the Paris Agreement and with the most recent scientific evidence.

item.title: A Global Database of Soil Methane Uptake (SMUD)
item.description:
A Global Database of Soil Methane Uptake (SMUD)
Jiawei Jiang, Zhifeng Yan, Jinshi Jian, Jesper Riis Christiansen, Xinchu Wang, Ren-Min Yang, Zhen Zhang, and Philippe Ciais
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6783–6797, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6783-2026, 2026
Soil methane uptake represents the second-largest sink of atmospheric methane but the field observations have not yet been systematically compiled. Here, we compiled an open global soil methane uptake database from the 1980s, covering most regions in multi-timescale along with the soil moisture and temperature data. The data show strong seasonal changes and different controls across biomes, helping improve climate estimates, models, and satellite evaluations.

item.title: OceanTACO: a multi-sensor global ocean sea surface state dataset
item.description:
OceanTACO: a multi-sensor global ocean sea surface state dataset
Nils Lehmann, Cesar Aybar, Ando Shah, Marcello Passaro, Jonathan L. Bamber, and Xiao Xiang Zhu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6815–6840, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6815-2026, 2026
Different satellites, ocean floats and model reanalysis products record sea surface height, temperature, salt content and winds, but each archive stores its data differently, so combining them is tedious and time consuming. We therefore combine these data sources into a consistent collection, so that data retrieval across sources becomes easier. Ocean studies are consequently easier to reproduce and compare, and hopefully support research and better understanding of ocean and climate processes.
